newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called higher with cash, natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called higher with cash, natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open higher Thursday based on the persistent strength in the western cash power market and natural gas futures, market sources said.

Despite more power plants set to return on-line led by San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) units in California, the power complex is taking cue from bullish short-term signals, market source said.

In over-the-counter business, August Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $35.45-$35.75 a megawatt hour (MWh) compared with Wednesday's settlement at $34.67, and August California-Oregon Border (COB) was discussed at $21.85-$22.00 slightly firmer than yesterday's close at $21.62.
Day-ahead firm, peak power prices at PV rose three to five dollars to $49.00-52.00 a MWh in early trading due to triple-digit heat smothering parts of the Southwest.
NYMEX August Henry Hub natural gas futures opened up 4.1 cents at $2.215 per million British thermal units amid concerns of a tropical depression forming in the Gulf of Mexcio.
The 1,070 megawatt (MW) SONGS unit 2, in San Clemente. Calif., synchronized to the grid Wednesday and scheduled to reach full output sometime today.
According to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, SONGS unit 2 was operating at 70 percent power as of this morning.
The adjoining 1,080 MW SONGS unit 3 was scheduled to be place online today.
In Richland, Washington, output at the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant achieved to 87 percent early Thursday.
The 750 MW Mohave coal-fired unit 3 was shut Monday for repairs and expected to resume operation Saturday.
The 550 MW unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired complex in Wyoming may restart today.
The 254 MW Valmy coal-fired unit 1 in Nevada will unlikely return to full power until the weekend after its output was halved Tuesday because of a tube leak.
Forecasters called for normal temperatures to continue across the Pacific Northwest into next week, and hot but seasonal weather over most of the Southwest.

Separately, southbound capacity of the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie transmission system was set to be cut by 250 MW to 3,200 MW between 0900 and 1600 PDT on today and Friday for maintenance work.
